_about: Regression evals for oak-quality-standards. 'trigger_evals' test that the skill description fires for reviewing/QA/auditing content against Oak's standards and not for near-misses (create-from-scratch, pure brand visuals, pure copy). 'quality_evals' are graded with assertions, comparing a with-skill run against a no-skill baseline. Re-run when the skill or the base model changes.

trigger_evals.query: Review this Year 7 science slide deck against Oak's quality standards and tell me what would fail.
Is this lesson up to Oak standard? QA it for me.
Audit this starter quiz against the rubric.
Check this worksheet meets Oak's bar before I publish it.
Run a quality review of this PE lesson guide — it's practical PE.
Which of Oak's required standards does this video clip miss?
Build me a Year 4 maths lesson on equivalent fractions.
What are Oak's brand colours and logo clearspace rules?
Rewrite this newsletter intro so it sounds like Oak.
Plan a year's worth of units for KS3 history.
trigger_evals.note: curriculum mapping/planning, not a standards review

quality_evals.prompt: Review this lesson slide deck against Oak's quality standards. DECK: opens straight on a content slide (no title slide); no keywords slide; bold is used throughout the body for emphasis; one check-for-understanding multiple-choice item whose options are 'A 10, B 100, C a lot'; a diagram that distinguishes 'safe' vs 'unsafe' only by green and red; no summary slide at the end.
assertions: scopes the review to the slide deck component before judging
classifies findings as Met / Partially met / Not met / Not applicable
flags the missing title slide (TS3) and missing summary slide (TS3)
flags bold used beyond keywords (TS2)
flags the guessable / minimally-different CfU options (PQ3 / 'not possible to guess the correct answer')
flags colour-only meaning in the safe/unsafe diagram and links it to the accessibility/dual-coding standard
separates Required-standard failures (blocking) from Model Practice recommendations
gives a concrete fix for each gap rather than only listing problems
is honest that this is an AI review, not an official Oak quality decision

quality_evals.prompt: QA this prior-knowledge starter quiz against Oak's standards. It has 8 questions; none of them check a keyword/vocabulary; question 1 is the hardest and they get easier; two questions have no hint; one image has no alt text.
assertions: scopes to the quiz and uses the quiz / pedagogical-quiz standards
flags the question count against Oak's expected number (6, or the subject-specific count)
flags that no question checks keyword/vocabulary (PQ4)
flags that challenge should increase, not decrease, with question number (PQ5)
flags the missing hints (every quiz question includes one relevant hint)
flags the missing alt text (TQ1 / accessibility)
marks Required failures as blocking and gives concrete fixes
notes it could ground the review in a real Oak quiz if the Oak Curriculum MCP were connected

quality_evals.prompt: Review this lesson video against Oak's quality standards. VIDEO: 12 minutes long; the first 20 seconds is the teacher talking over the title slide; there is no picture-in-picture of the teacher at any point; a demonstration clip has correct/incorrect technique distinguished only by a red and a green tick; the teacher says 'as we saw in the Year 8 lesson on forces'; no OGL slide at the end.
assertions: scopes the review to the video component and loads the video standards
flags the length against Oak's 20-35 minute expectation (TV1)
flags the missing picture-in-picture / PiP coverage (TV1)
flags the title-slide opening having narration in the first five seconds (TV1)
flags the reference to another lesson / key stage in the video (TV3)
flags the missing OGL end slide (TV1)
flags the colour-only correct/incorrect distinction and links it to the accessibility/dual-coding standard
separates Required failures (blocking) from Model Practice and gives a concrete fix for each
is explicit that it is an AI review for a human to sign off

quality_evals.prompt: Review this worksheet against Oak's quality standards. WORKSHEET: text is mid-grey to look softer; tasks are labelled Task 1, Task 2 (not A, B) and the slide deck calls them Task A and Task B; it is four sides of A4; one task is multiple choice; there is no separate worksheet answers document though the tasks require written answers.
assertions: scopes the review to the worksheet (and worksheet answers) component
flags worksheet text not being black for printing (TW1)
flags the task labelling / titles not matching the slide deck (TW1 / resource consistency)
flags multiple-choice questions being used in a practice task
flags the length against the 'no more than two sides of A4 wherever possible' standard
flags the missing worksheet answers document for written tasks
separates Required failures from Model Practice and gives concrete fixes
is honest that this is an AI review, not an official Oak quality decision
